From a non-European Union state

existing.eligibility_summary: First-time applicants to Sciences Po from a non-European Union state whose household does not file taxes within the European Union, admitted to the Undergraduate College or to a two-year Master's programme. Applicants who are already enrolled at Sciences Po cannot apply.
benefits: Undergraduate College: either a total exemption or an exemption of €9,500 from tuition fees
Master's: €18,500 exemption from tuition fees for each of the two years of the Master's programme
Automatic renewal for holders continuing to graduate study at Sciences Po
requirements: Declare the Émile Boutmy scholarship in the 'Financial information' section of the Sciences Po application before the application deadline
Attach the applicable language test results by the scholarship application deadline
Submit only complete files — 'We will only take into account complete files'
documents: Sciences Po application with the Émile Boutmy scholarship declared in the 'Financial information' section
Language test results, if applicable to the Master's programme
For candidates applying via Parcoursup: online Admission Office form after Parcoursup validation
Dated and signed scholarship certificate, uploaded in the student portal during administrative registration
application_method: Undergraduate College applicants from foreign secondary schools: tick the Émile Boutmy scholarship in the 'Financial information' section of the Sciences Po application
Undergraduate College applicants from French secondary schools: complete the Admission Office online form once the Parcoursup application has been validated
Master's applicants: tick the Émile Boutmy scholarship in the 'Financial information' section of the Sciences Po application and attach the language test if applicable
existing.selection_notes: Awarded on merit and according to the type of profile sought; the allocation is intrinsically linked to the admissions process and the excellence criteria are evaluated solely within the review of the application. Only admitted students' files are reviewed.
existing.best_fit: Non-EU nationals with strong secondary or undergraduate records whose household has no EU tax residence and who apply to the Undergraduate College or a two-year Master's at Sciences Po.
existing.notes: The Boutmy scholarship is linked to the programme of study at the time of admission; enrolling directly in a dual degree in the third year loses the award. It cannot be combined with any other scholarship awarded by Sciences Po and its partners (Mastercard, CARE, Fondation de France/René Seydoux, China Scholarship Council), but may be combined with external scholarships (Eiffel, AEFE, French government scholarships).
existing.duration: Bachelor's: tuition-fee grant for the first year, retained during the third year abroad. Master's: €18,500 tuition-fee exemption for each of the two years of the programme.
existing.application_period: Tied to the Sciences Po admission cycle for the 2027 entry; applicants declare the scholarship inside the Sciences Po application.
existing.deadline_display: Deadline for undergraduate programme (applicants from foreign secondary schools): January 13, 2027 (results in April). Deadline for undergraduate programme (applicants from French secondary schools): April 1st, 2027. Deadline for master programme: 18 October (1st committee, results before December 20) or 29 November (2nd committee, results before March 2).
existing.program_type: Tuition-fee exemption awarded to admitted first-time international students of the Undergraduate College and the two-year Master's

existing.description: Here, you can find more information about Campus France, other external scholarships, and various loan opportunities to finance your education at HEC Paris.
eligibility: Admitted, or applying, to an HEC Paris Master's programme or the MBA
Most merit-based awards require a non-French diploma (Bachelor's or Master's)
Equal Opportunity need-based award: non-French nationality only, and not for candidates already studying in France
AVENIR: Spanish and French-Spanish candidates
Future Leaders of Africa: citizens of South Africa, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya or Uganda with a degree obtained outside France
30% CLUB: female candidates with a non-French diploma applying in Round 2
Women's High Potential: female candidates with a non-French diploma
VOLKSWAGEN Women in Leadership: German-speaking female students interested in the automobile industry
Wonder Woman: female candidates of Indian nationality or Indian heritage
Women in Finance & Technology: female students who can demonstrate proficiency in French
Chalhoub Group: nationals of Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain, Lebanon, Syria, Qatar, Egypt, Yemen, Jordan, Oman, Iran, Iraq or Palestine
Garzouzi Foundation: Lebanese nationality, under 25 on September 1st of the year of admission, clean criminal record, relevant social criteria
Imagine Fellowship: candidates from countries or states affected by war and/or armed conflict
Eiffel Excellence: non-French candidates under 29 who have not previously been rejected and do not already hold another French government scholarship
Lafayette Fellowship: 27 or younger on July 1st, 2026, bachelor's degree from a U.S. institution completed between August 2023 and June 2026 with a GPA of at least 3.7/4.0
existing.eligibility_summary: Merit-based awards are considered automatically for applicants admitted to HEC Paris Master's programmes, most of them requiring a non-French diploma; need-based awards require non-French nationality or a specific nationality and are submitted through the HEC Paris Applicant Space. Several named awards are restricted by gender, nationality, field or sport.
benefits: HEC Foundation Excellence Scholarship: up to €15,000 tuition-fee reduction
Women's High Potential Scholarship: up to €15,000
VOLKSWAGEN HEC Women in Leadership Scholarship: up to €15,000
Future Leaders of Africa: up to €15,000
Women in Finance & Technology Scholarship: up to €20,000
Stan Schwab Scholarship for Athletic and Academic Achievements: €10,000
Equal Opportunity Scholarship: up to 35% of tuition fees
Garzouzi Foundation Scholarship: €15,000 in M1 and a further €15,000 in M2
coverage: No living-cost allowance from HEC's own merit-based awards
requirements: Submit the initial Master's application first — 'You can start your needs-based scholarship application ONLY once you submit your initial master's application!'
Complete the Needs-Based Scholarship Form in the HEC Paris Applicant Space before the round's noon deadline
Attach the award-specific essay or documents where required
documents: Needs-Based Scholarship Form completed in the HEC Paris Applicant Space
350-word essay where the named award requires one
Clean criminal record in PDF emailed to scholarships@hec.fr (Garzouzi)
Proof of parents' income and sports licence with athletic achievements (Stan Schwab)
French proficiency test (DALF, TCF or TEF at C1–C2) for non-native French speakers under the Women in Finance & Technology award
application_method: Merit-based awards: no separate application for most awards — 'All admitted students will be considered automatically'
Need-based awards: submit the Needs-Based Scholarship Form in the HEC Paris Applicant Space
Award-specific essays and documents emailed to scholarships@hec.fr
existing.selection_notes: Merit-based decisions rest on academic excellence, the overall strength of the application, interview performance and GMAT/GRE/TAGE-MAGE performance; scholarship decisions are emailed within one week of the publication of admission results.
existing.best_fit: Strong-academic international applicants to HEC Paris Master's programmes who apply in one of the four admissions rounds and, for need-based awards, can document limited financial means or an eligible nationality.
existing.notes: The need-based deadlines are 12pm noon Paris time on each round date. 'All bursaries allocated with be automatically suspended if any information communicated by the candidate is found to be false.' The Eiffel Excellence Scholarship and the Lafayette Fellowship are third-party awards that HEC pre-selects for or hosts, and the Eiffel programme explicitly does not pay tuition fees.
existing.duration: One admission cycle; the Garzouzi award can be renewed for a second Master's year subject to GPA and foundation approval.
existing.application_period: Admissions Round 1 through Round 4 of the HEC Paris Master's cycle, with the need-based form due at noon on each round's deadline.
existing.deadline_display: Need-based scholarship form deadlines: Round 1 – October 26th, 2026 at 12pm (noon); Round 2 – December 21st, 2026 at 12pm (noon); Round 3 – March 16th, 2027 at 12pm (noon); Round 4 – May 18th, 2027 at 12pm (noon).
existing.program_type: Merit-based and need-based tuition-fee reduction scholarships for HEC Paris Master's and MBA admissions
